body.en: The interquartile range Q3 − Q1 covers the middle half of the values. Half of it is the *quartile deviation*, or semi-interquartile range. For an individual or discrete series, Q1 is the size of the (N + 1)/4th item and Q3 of the 3(N + 1)/4th item; for a continuous series use N/4 and 3N/4 with the interpolation formula. Because it ignores the lowest and highest quarters, QD is not affected by extreme values and can be found for open-ended classes.

points.en: Unaffected by extremes; ignores half the data

say.en: The interquartile range Q3 - Q1 covers the middle half of the values. Half of it is the quartile deviation, or semi-interquartile range. For an individual or discrete series, Q1 is the size of the N plus 1/4th item and Q3 of the 3N plus 1/4th item; for a continuous series use N over 4 and 3N/4 with the interpolation formula. Because it ignores the lowest and highest quarters, QD is not affected by extreme values and can be found for open-ended classes. QD equals (Q3 - Q1)/2.
Coefficient of QD equals (Q3 - Q1)/Q3 plus Q1.

body.en: The *mean deviation* is the arithmetic mean of the absolute deviations of the values from an average, usually the mean or the median. Signs are ignored, because the plain deviations from the mean add to zero. It is least when taken about the median. MD uses every value, so it is more representative than range or QD, but ignoring signs makes it unsuitable for further algebra. Its coefficient is MD divided by the average used.

points.en: MD = Σ|x − A|/N, where A is the mean or median
For a frequency series: Σf|x − A|/Σf

prompt.en: Arrange the steps to find the quartile deviation of an individual series.

steps.en: Arrange the values in ascending order
Find the (N + 1)/4th item: this is Q1
Find the 3(N + 1)/4th item: this is Q3
Subtract: Q3 − Q1 is the interquartile range
Halve it to get the quartile deviation

problem.en: Find the mean deviation about the median of: 5, 8, 12, 15, 20.

steps.en: The values are already in order; the median is the 3rd item, 12.

answer.en: MD about the median = 4.4; coefficient of MD = 0.37.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Find the mean deviation about the median of: 5, 8, 12, 15, 20.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Find the mean deviation about the median of: 5, 8, 12, 15, 20.
The values are already in order; the median is the 3rd item, 12.
Absolute deviations from 12: 7, 4, 0, 3, 8.
Their sum is 22.
MD equals 22 over 5 equals 4.4; coefficient equals 4.4 over 12 equals 0.37.
So the answer is MD about the median equals 4.4; coefficient of MD equals 0.37.
